title: NEET UG 2026 Counselling: What NRI and OCI Candidates Need to Know About Eligibility
excerpt: MCC has issued a notice requiring NRI and OCI candidates to verify their credentials with the NRI Document Verification Team before proceeding with NEET UG 2026 counselling for deemed university MBBS seats.
body:
• The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has issued a notice requiring NRI and OCI candidates to get their credentials verified by the MCC's NRI Document Verification Team before proceeding with counselling.
  • Round 1 registration for NEET UG 2026 counselling opened on August 5 at mcc.nic.in, with the registration deadline on August 12 for the first round.
  • NRI/OCI candidates applying to deemed universities need a sponsor's passport copy, embassy certificate, sponsorship affidavit, and relationship affidavit — all documents must be verified before seat allotment.
  • Deemed university seats carry a registration fee of ₹5,000 plus a refundable security deposit of ₹2,00,000, totaling ₹2,05,000.

MCC Issues Verification Notice

The Medical Counselling Committee, operating under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), has added a verification step specifically for NRI and OCI candidates seeking MBBS and BDS seats through the NEET UG 2026 counselling process. In a notice issued on August 8, the MCC stated that NRI and OCI candidates must first get their credentials verified by the MCC's NRI Document Verification Team to determine their eligibility before they can participate in seat allotment.

This verification requirement is separate from the standard document upload during registration and applies specifically to candidates seeking admission under the NRI quota at deemed universities participating in the centralized counselling process.

Documents NRI and OCI Candidates Must Prepare

The documentation requirements for NRI and OCI candidates go beyond the standard set needed by general category applicants. In addition to the usual NEET admit card, scorecard, and Class 10 and 12 certificates, NRI/OCI candidates must submit:

Sponsorship documents: A duly notarized sponsorship affidavit confirming that the sponsor will bear the candidate's educational and other expenses for the entire duration of the medical course. This is a critical document — incomplete or improperly notarized affidavits are a common reason for rejection.

Sponsor identity: A passport copy of the sponsor along with an embassy certificate (certificate from the consulate) establishing the sponsor's NRI status.

Relationship proof: A relationship affidavit establishing the connection between the candidate and the sponsor.

Candidate documents: OCI or PIO card of the candidate (if applicable), candidate's passport copy, sponsor's residence proof, and financial support documents.

Counselling Process and Fees

The NEET UG 2026 counselling is conducted by the MCC for 15% All India Quota seats, along with seats at AIIMS, JIPMER, central universities, and deemed universities. Round 1 registration opened on August 5, with candidates registering and filling choices through the MCC portal at mcc.nic.in.

The fee structure differs significantly between government and deemed university seats. For government and central university AIQ seats, general/EWS candidates pay ₹1,000 in non-refundable registration fees plus ₹10,000 as refundable security deposit. SC/ST/OBC/PwD candidates pay ₹500 plus ₹5,000. Deemed university candidates across all categories face a substantially higher outlay: ₹5,000 registration fee plus ₹2,00,000 security deposit, totaling ₹2,05,000.

The counselling process includes Round 1, Round 2, Round 3, and a Stray Vacancy Round. Candidates not allotted a seat in initial rounds can continue participating in subsequent rounds per MCC eligibility guidelines.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

MCC has highlighted several documentation errors that can lead to cancellation of deemed university seats. These include uploading blurred or old photographs, name mismatches across certificates, using expired OBC or EWS certificates, incorrect category selection during registration, and carrying a different ID proof than the one uploaded during the application process.

For NRI/OCI candidates specifically, the sponsorship affidavit must clearly cover the entire course duration — not just the first year. The embassy certificate must be current, and all documents must be in English or accompanied by notarized translations.

Key Deadlines and Next Steps

Candidates should monitor the MCC portal regularly for seat matrix releases, choice-locking deadlines, and allotment results. Once choices are locked, they generally cannot be modified for that counselling round, so preferences should be reviewed carefully before final submission. Seat allotment results are typically released within five to seven days of each round's commencement.

For NRI families navigating this process from abroad, the MCC's NRI verification requirement adds a time-sensitive step. Candidates should ensure all documents are prepared, notarized, and submitted for verification as early as possible to avoid delays that could affect their participation in seat allotment rounds.
nri_angle: NRI and OCI families with children seeking MBBS seats in India must navigate MCC's verification process — sponsorship affidavits and embassy certificates are mandatory.
